hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: Sort all meetings by their ending timestamps in ascending sequence.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: For each meeting [start, end, earn], find the latest preceding compatible meeting ending before start minus gap.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Transition either by taking the current meeting plus previous optimal earnings or skipping the current meeting.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect

def maxMeetingEarnings(meetings: list[list[int]], gap: int) -> int:
    # Each meeting: [start, end, earnings]
    meetings.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
    n = len(meetings)

    dp = [0] * (n + 1)
    ends = [m[1] for m in meetings]

    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        start, end, earn = meetings[i - 1]
        # Find latest meeting ending <= start - gap
        idx = bisect.bisect_right(ends, start - gap)
        dp[i] = max(dp[i - 1], earn + dp[idx])

    return dp[n]
```

complexity.notes: Sorting intervals and binary searching the latest compatible non-overlapping predecessor.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Exhaustive subset generation is exponential in the number of meetings.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: DP array and sorted endpoints use O(n) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Combines interval sorting with binary search predecessor lookup.
